home.title: Free Weight Loss Tracker: Weight, BMI and Goals | Weightloss Tracker
home.desc: Free weight loss tracker: log your weight and see weekly trends, BMI, estimated body fat and your goal date. No food logging. Made for GLP-1 users.
home.h1: See your weight loss progress clearly, week after week
home.lead: Weightloss Tracker is a free web app for people who want to watch their weight come down steadily, without counting calories or logging food. Log your weight in seconds and see your trend, BMI, a body fat estimate, your goal date and the milestones you have reached.
home.badge.nopw: No password: sign in with an email code, Google or Microsoft
home.badge.browser: Works on phone, tablet and computer
home.glance.p: Everything is worked out from the weights and measurements you enter. These screens use demo data.
home.glance.1: Charts by week, month, year or all time
home.glance.2: Your goal, progress and an estimated date to reach it
home.who.1.p: You don't need a food diary. You want to see that your weight is coming down steadily and that the rest of your body is changing with it.
home.who.2.h: Anyone losing weight at a steady pace
home.who.2.p: Weigh in when it suits you, once a day or once a week, and let the charts show the trend instead of one day's number.
home.who.3.p: No calories, no barcode scanning, no social feed. Just your weight, your body figures and your goal.
home.glp.h: Made for GLP-1 weight loss: progress, not calories
home.glp.p1: When you take a GLP-1 medication, what matters is not what you ate today but whether your weight is coming down week by week, and how your body is changing as it does. Weightloss Tracker shows exactly that.
home.glp.l1: Weekly trend: a chart of how much your weight changed each week, so a steady pace is easy to see.
home.glp.l2: Body changes: BMI, a body fat estimate, tape measurements, and readings from your smart scale that you record in the app.
home.glp.l3: Goal and milestones: your progress towards your target weight, an estimated date to reach it, and badges as you pass each milestone.
home.glp.p2: There is nothing to log except your weight, and your measurements if you want to.
home.how.1.p: Enter your email address and type in the 6-digit code we send you, or continue with Google or Microsoft.
home.how.2.h: Add your details and a first weight
home.how.2.p: Your height and age let the app work out your BMI, a body fat estimate and an ideal weight range.
home.how.3.h: Set a goal and keep logging
home.how.3.p: Choose a target weight and date. Each weigh-in updates your charts, goal progress, streak and milestones.
home.feat.1.p: Log today's weight or add past dates, in kg, lb or stone. See every entry with the change from the one before.
home.feat.2.p: Weekly, 30-day, 90-day, monthly, yearly and all-time views, plus your average weekly loss.
home.feat.3.p: Target weight and date, a progress bar and an estimated achievement date based on your recent weeks.
home.feat.4.h: Estimated body fat and fat loss
home.feat.4.p: No smart scale needed: from your weight, height and age the app estimates your body fat and how much of your loss is fat.
home.feat.5.p: Tape measurements, and readings from your smart scale (body fat, water, muscle and bone) that you record yourself, with insights as they change.
home.feat.6.p: Milestone badges, a weekly streak, and an optional weekly reminder and monthly progress email.
home.why.p1: I'm on a GLP-1 medication, and I wanted to focus on my weight loss and my health improvements, not on tracking food and calories. I needed a simple way to see that the loss was steady and that my body was improving as the weight came off. I wanted to know:
home.why.l1: how my weight was trending week to week
home.why.l2: whether I was on track for my goal, and roughly when I would reach it
home.why.l3: how my BMI, body fat estimate and measurements were changing
home.why.l4: which milestones I had already passed
home.why.p2: Seeing those numbers move a little each week kept me motivated to keep a steady pace. I have lost over 20 kg, and the app is free for anyone who wants the same.
faq.free.a: Yes. There is no paid plan and there are no adverts inside the app. It runs in your web browser, so there is nothing to install.
faq.glp.q: Is it suitable if I'm taking a GLP-1 medication?
faq.glp.a: Yes. That is why it was built. It doesn't ask you to log food or count calories. It tracks your progress: your weekly weight trend, your BMI and body fat estimate, your measurements, your goal and the milestones you reach, so you can see that your weight loss is steady.
faq.food.q: Do I have to log food or calories?
faq.food.a: No. Weightloss Tracker has no food diary and no calorie counting. You log your weight, and if you like, body measurements and smart-scale readings.
faq.signin.a: There is no password. Enter your email address and we send you a 6-digit code that works for 15 minutes, or continue with your Google or Microsoft account. You stay signed in on that device until you sign out, for up to 30 days between visits and at most 90 days in total.
faq.units.a: Weight in kilograms, pounds or stone (shown as stone and pounds, for example 12 st 7.0 lb), and height in centimetres, metres or feet and inches. Body measurements are in centimetres. You can change units at any time in Settings.
faq.lang.a: The app and this website are in English, German, Spanish and French. You choose the app's language in Settings. Reminder and report emails are currently sent in English.
faq.email.a: Only to send your sign-in codes, unless you choose more. In Settings you can turn on a weekly reminder on the day and time you pick, and a monthly progress report sent on the 1st of each month. Both are off until you turn them on.
faq.past.q: Can I add weights from before I started?
faq.past.a: Yes. When you add an entry you can pick any past date, so you can fill in your history. You can also delete any entry.
faq.bodyfat.q: How is the body fat estimate worked out?
faq.bodyfat.a: From your BMI and age, using the Deurenberg formula. The app doesn't ask for your sex, so the Health tab shows a range between the male and female results. It is an estimate; if you have a smart scale, you can also type in its body fat reading.
faq.device.q: Is there an app to download?
faq.device.a: No download is needed. Weightloss Tracker is a website that works in the browser on your phone, tablet or computer, and you can add it to your home screen. It needs an internet connection.
faq.data.a: Only you. We don't sell your data or share your tracking data with anyone. The privacy page explains what is stored and how to have it deleted.
faq.scale.q: Does it connect to my smart scale?
faq.scale.a: It doesn't connect to scales or sync with them. You record readings from your smart scale (body fat, water, muscle and bone, as percentages) on the Body tab yourself, and the app shows how they change over time.
features.title: Features: Weight Log, Charts, Goals and BMI | Weightloss Tracker
features.desc: Weight log in kg, lb or stone, charts, goal date, BMI, estimated body fat and fat loss, measurements, milestones and email reminders.
features.lead: Weightloss Tracker keeps to the numbers that show real progress. Here is everything it does today. The screenshots use demo data.
features.log.p: Log your current weight in a couple of taps, or add an entry for any past date to fill in your history.
features.log.l1: Kilograms, pounds or stone, switchable at any time
features.log.l2: History table with the date, weight and change from the entry before
features.log.l3: Delete any entry you didn't mean to add
features.charts.p: Recent views keep you on track week to week; the All Time view shows the whole journey from your first weigh-in.
features.charts.l1: Recent: weekly, 30 days and 90 days, with buttons to step back through earlier periods
features.charts.l2: Long term: monthly, yearly and all time
features.charts.l3: Average weekly loss and a 6-month projection based on your trend so far
features.goals.p: Set a target weight and date. The Goals tab shows how far you have come and, once you have at least three entries, when you are likely to get there at your current pace.
features.goals.l2: Estimated achievement date from your average weekly loss over the last 8 weeks
features.goals.l3: Consistency score and a prediction for your next check-in
features.health.p: From your height, age and latest weight the Health tab works out:
features.health.l1: BMI and its category, plus a figure adjusted for your body frame
features.health.l2: Body fat estimate, shown as a range
features.health.l4: General, research-based estimates of how health typically improves with weight loss, each with the study it draws on
features.est.h: Estimated body fat and fat loss: no smart scale needed
features.est.p: You don't need special equipment to see more than your weight. From your weight, height and age the app estimates:
features.est.l1: Your body fat percentage, using the Deurenberg formula (shown as a range, because the app doesn't ask for your sex), with a chart of how it changes
features.est.l2: How much of the weight you have lost is likely to be fat
features.est.l3: These estimates were checked against real smart-scale readings. They are estimates, not measurements.
features.ben.p: The Health tab shows general, research-based estimates of how health typically improves as weight comes down, for type 2 diabetes, blood pressure, sleep apnoea, fatty liver, heart health, mood and joints, each with the study it draws on. They describe what typically happens with weight loss; they are not a diagnosis or a measurement of your own health.
features.ben.src.p: Some of the published evidence on weight loss and health:
src.dpp: Type 2 diabetes: losing a modest amount of weight can prevent or delay type 2 diabetes. NIDDK, Diabetes Prevention Program.
src.bp: Blood pressure: weight loss lowers blood pressure. Neter et al., Hypertension, 2003 (meta-analysis of 25 trials).
src.osa: Sleep apnoea: losing weight is one of the recommended lifestyle changes. NHS, Sleep apnoea.
src.liver: Fatty liver: losing weight can reduce fat in the liver and help repair damage. NHS, Non-alcoholic fatty liver disease.
src.knee: Knee osteoarthritis: weight loss improved pain and function. Messier et al., JAMA, 2013 (IDEA trial).
src.mood: Mood: weight-loss programmes reduced symptoms of depression. Fabricatore et al., International Journal of Obesity, 2011.
src.bmi: BMI categories: World Health Organization, Obesity and overweight fact sheet.
src.deur: Body fat estimate: Deurenberg et al., British Journal of Nutrition, 1991.
features.body.p: Weight isn't the only sign of progress. On the Body tab you can keep a history of:
features.body.l1: Tape measurements in centimetres: neck, chest, waist, hips, thighs, calves and arms
features.body.l2: Record readings from your smart scale: body fat, water, muscle and bone, as percentages
features.body.l3: Insights that explain how each figure is changing
features.ach.p: Small wins keep you going. As your weight comes down you unlock milestone badges, nine levels in your chosen unit (from 1 kg up to 50 kg, or the same in pounds or stone).
features.ach.l1: Weekly streak: current and longest run of weeks with a weigh-in
features.ach.l2: Goals achieved this week, month and year
features.ach.l3: Your total loss compared with everyday objects
features.email.p: Both are optional and off until you turn them on in Settings.
features.email.l1: Weekly reminder on the day and time you choose, in your time zone
features.email.l2: Monthly progress report on the 1st of each month
features.settings.l1: Weight in kg, lb or stone; height in cm, m or feet and inches
features.settings.l4: UK, US, ISO or European date format, and your time zone
features.signin.l1: No password to remember: a 6-digit email code that works for 15 minutes
features.signin.l2: Or continue with Google or Microsoft
features.signin.l3: Stay signed in on your device for 30 days after your last visit, up to 90 days after you sign in
features.signin.l4: Repeated wrong codes are blocked to keep your account safe
features.free.p: No paid plan, no adverts inside the app and nothing to install.
about.title: About: Why I Built Weightloss Tracker | Weightloss Tracker
about.desc: Why Weightloss Tracker exists: built by someone on GLP-1 medication who wanted to see steady progress, not count calories. How the app grew, one need at a time.
about.lead: A simple tracker for steady weight loss, built one need at a time.
about.start.p1: I wanted to focus on two things: the weight I was losing and the improvements in my health. Not on tracking food and calories. I'm on a GLP-1 medication, so the eating side was already taken care of. What I needed was a simple way to see that my body was improving as I lost weight, and that the loss stayed steady.
about.start.p2: Nothing I tried did just that, so I built it myself. Every feature came from something I wanted to know about my own progress.
about.s1.h: A weight log, a goal and the first health figures
about.s1.p: It began with the basics: log a weight, keep a history, set a target. Straight away I added BMI, a body fat estimate and an ideal weight range, because I wanted to know whether my body was getting healthier, not just lighter.
about.s2.h: Charts: this week and the whole journey
about.s2.p: One day's number jumps around, so next came the charts. The recent views (weekly, 30 days and 90 days) kept me on track week to week. The All Time view, right from my first weigh-in, showed how far I had come.
about.s3.h: What the loss means for health
about.s3.p: I wanted to know what losing weight meant for my health, not just the number on the scale. So I built the Health tab around published research on how health typically improves with weight loss: type 2 diabetes, blood pressure, sleep apnoea, fatty liver, heart health, mood and joints. It gives general estimates for your BMI, each shown with the study it draws on, not a measurement of your own health.
about.s4.p: I added kilograms, pounds and stone, and sign-in with Google or Microsoft, so it took seconds to open the app and log a weight.
about.s5.p: A steady pace needs regular weigh-ins, so I added an optional weekly reminder email and a monthly progress report. At the same time the app learned German, Spanish and French.
about.s6.p: I wanted to know whether I was on course for my goal and when I would get there. The Goals tab gained an estimated achievement date, a consistency score, a weekly streak and my average weekly loss. Seeing the streak grow and the date hold kept me going at a steady pace.
about.s7.p: Some weeks I wasn't noticing the loss physically, even when the scale said it was happening. So I added a Body tab for tape measurements, with insights that show how each one is changing. When the scale is slow, the tape measure often isn't.
about.s8.p: I was also using a smart scale to understand what was happening inside: body fat, water, muscle and bone. So I added a place in the app to record those readings and see how they change over time.
about.s9.p: Not everyone has a smart scale. I used my own smart-scale readings to check and fine-tune the app's estimates, which start from standard published formulas. So anyone can see an estimated body fat percentage and estimated fat loss from just their weight, height and age. They are estimates, not measurements.
about.now.p: Weightloss Tracker is free and runs in any web browser. Today it has:
about.now.l1: a weight log in kg, lb or stone, with past dates
about.now.l2: charts from weekly to all time, average weekly loss and a 6-month projection
about.now.l3: goals with an estimated achievement date, milestone badges and a weekly streak
about.now.l4: BMI, a body fat estimate, an ideal weight range and general health estimates
about.now.l5: tape measurements, and a place to record smart-scale readings, with insights
about.now.l6: optional weekly reminder and monthly report emails
about.now.l7: English, German, Spanish and French, and six colour themes
about.now.l8: sign-in with an email code, Google or Microsoft: no password
about.result.p: I have lost over 20 kg. Watching the numbers move each week is what kept me motivated, and I hope it helps you keep a steady pace too.
how.title: How It Works: Start Tracking Your Weight Loss | Weightloss Tracker
how.desc: Get started with Weightloss Tracker in a few minutes: sign in with an email code, Google or Microsoft, add your details, log a weight, set a goal and choose reminders.
how.lead: You can be set up in a few minutes. Here is what happens, step by step.
how.1.h: Sign in or create an account
how.1.p: Type your email address and we send you a 6-digit code (it is also in the email's subject line). Enter it and you are in. Or use your Google or Microsoft account. No password is ever needed.
how.2.p: On the Data tab enter your height, age, body frame and activity level. These are used to work out your BMI, body fat estimate, ideal weight range and health figures.
how.3.p: Enter today's weight, or add entries for past dates if you already have a history. Use kg, lb or stone.
how.4.p: Choose a target weight and a date. After three entries the Goals tab estimates when you will reach your goal at your current pace.
how.5.p: Each weigh-in updates your charts, goal progress, weekly streak and milestones. The Health and Body tabs show how your BMI, body fat estimate and measurements are changing.
how.6.p: In Settings, turn on a weekly reminder for the day and time you prefer, and a monthly progress report. Change your units, language and theme here too.
how.tips.l1: Weigh yourself at about the same time of day, on the same scale.
how.tips.l2: Look at the weekly and monthly charts rather than a single day.
how.tips.l3: Add a few tape measurements now and then: they can change even in a week when the scale doesn't.

bmi.title: Free BMI Calculator (kg, lb, stone, cm, ft) | Weightloss Tracker
bmi.desc: Work out your body mass index in seconds with metric or imperial units. The same BMI calculation Weightloss Tracker uses. Nothing you type is sent anywhere.
bmi.lead: Work out your body mass index (BMI). This is the same calculation Weightloss Tracker uses. It runs in your browser, so nothing you type is sent anywhere.
bmi.error: Please enter your height and weight.
bmi.about.p1: BMI is your weight in kilograms divided by your height in metres squared. For example, 80 kg and 1.75 m gives 80 ÷ (1.75 × 1.75) = 26.1.
bmi.about.p2: BMI is a quick, general guide for adults. It doesn't tell muscle from fat, so it can read high for very muscular people, and the categories are not meant for children.
bmi.track.p: One number is a snapshot. In Weightloss Tracker your BMI updates with every weigh-in, alongside a body fat estimate and your ideal weight range.
